site.name: stripe-docs
site.summary: stripe-docs-clone Clone of the Stripe Docs Hosted Checkout Quickstart tutorial area. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Quickstart home: three-column layout — left product / section navigation tree, central step-by-step tutorial (each step: explanation + multi-language switchable code block + copy button + Test / Live markers), right-side on-this-page outline (scroll-spy highlighting); top Stripe docs nav (Docs / API reference / Search / environment switch) | | `embedded.html` | Embedded checkout variant: iframe / element integration steps for embedding into a site | | `customization.html` | Branding and customization: colors, logo, domain, email, etc. |

run_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the full Stripe docs clone experience, centering on the hosted Checkout quickstart as the main journey, then validating adjacent embedded and customization docs flows, key interactive docs controls, and responsive behavior.
run_plan.summary: Start on the hosted quickstart and treat it as the primary documentation flow: verify navigation structure, tutorial progression, code example interactions, search/dialog behavior, and cross-links to adjacent local pages and external references. Then cover the embedded and customization pages to confirm the docs system stays consistent while content and guidance change appropriately. Finish with focused mobile checks on the most interaction-dense areas, especially navigation, code controls, dialog/search access, and small tap targets already flagged in prescan.
assumptions: The three local HTML pages are the full in-scope site surface: index.html, embedded.html, and customization.html.
The top nav, left section nav, right on-this-page outline, search trigger, and code-block controls are shared or substantially similar across pages.
External links to live Stripe docs and Dashboard are present for reference behavior, but the primary UX evaluation should stay focused on the local clone pages.
A dialog is present on each page and is likely related to search or another global utility because each page reports 1 dialog and a visible search trigger.
The hosted page contains multi-language switchable code blocks, copy buttons, and Test/Live markers as part of the main tutorial experience.
risk_hotspots: index.html: search trigger ('Search… /') and associated dialog open/close/focus behavior
index.html: multi-language code block tabs such as 'Node' and whether code content/state changes correctly
index.html: copy buttons in code examples, including feedback and repeated use across multiple snippets
index.html: right-side on-this-page outline / scroll-spy highlighting while traversing long tutorial content
index.html: long-page recovery/navigation using top nav, left nav, in-page outline, and end-of-page related cards
embedded.html: embedded-specific tutorial steps and whether code/examples clearly differ from hosted flow
customization.html: accuracy and clarity of customization constraints, especially branding/custom-domain guidance
Global external links: Official docs / Branding / Open source / official reference cards should behave consistently without breaking local navigation expectations
Mobile viewport: small tap targets already flagged for home link, breadcrumb/title link, copy buttons, Yes/No controls, and footer/reference links
Any page with many links/buttons and no forms: interaction affordance and state feedback may be subtle or easy to miss

phases.title: Primary hosted quickstart baseline
phases.objective: Validate the main docs journey on the hosted Checkout page, including page structure, shared navigation, and the core tutorial reading flow.
key_checks: Confirm the hosted page loads as the default entry and that top nav, left rail, main content, and right-side outline are all present and understandable.
Traverse the hosted tutorial from hero/intro through the major steps such as SDK install, Session creation, storefront post, and webhook fulfillment guidance.
Check that top navigation highlights or otherwise indicates the current section/page appropriately for Hosted.
Use the left navigation items for local page movement and verify the current-page treatment for 'Hosted quickstart'.
Check end-of-page related cards/links that point to embedded.html and customization.html for sensible adjacent-flow handoff.
exit_criteria: The hosted page's information architecture and primary reading path are understood from top to bottom.
At least one path each is confirmed for top-nav, left-nav, and in-content/local related-navigation movement from the hosted page.

phases.title: Hosted interactive docs controls
phases.objective: Exercise the interaction-heavy controls on the hosted page that are most likely to fail or create UX friction in a docs/tutorial interface.
key_checks: Open the search control ('Search… /') and validate whether a dialog appears, whether focus lands correctly, and whether it can be dismissed reliably.
If keyboard shortcut support is available from the visible hint ('/'), verify whether slash opens search without disrupting page content.
Interact with language/code tabs beginning with the visible 'Node' button and check whether code content, active states, and any test/live markers update coherently.
Use multiple copy buttons across different code snippets and verify feedback state, repeatability, and whether copied content appears to match the visible snippet.
Observe any sticky or scroll-spy behavior in the right-side outline while scrolling through the long hosted tutorial.
Check any visible binary controls such as Yes/No near the bottom area for clear state change and adequate feedback.
exit_criteria: Search/dialog behavior has been opened and closed successfully at least once.
At least two code-related interactions are validated, including tab switching and copy behavior.
The on-this-page outline or equivalent in-page navigation has been observed during scroll.

phases.title: Adjacent local docs flows
phases.objective: Cover the two adjacent local pages and verify that each preserves the shared docs shell while presenting meaningfully distinct guidance.
key_checks: Open embedded.html through local navigation and confirm the page clearly shifts from hosted redirect flow to embedded page guidance.
On embedded.html, verify major steps such as server SDK/Stripe.js setup, embedded Session creation, mounting embedded Checkout, and return-page guidance are discoverable and coherent.
Open customization.html and verify it clearly frames what Checkout can and cannot be customized, rather than implying unsupported controls.
On customization.html, inspect sections around branding settings, text/policies/support details, blocked card brands, and custom domains for clear boundaries and internal consistency.
Across both pages, confirm top nav/left nav/current-page indicators stay consistent and allow easy movement back to hosted.
exit_criteria: Both adjacent local pages have been visited and scrolled enough to validate their main step structure.
The differences between hosted, embedded, and customization guidance are explicitly confirmed through content and navigation behavior.

phases.title: Cross-link integrity and recovery paths
phases.objective: Check how users recover, compare, and branch between local pages and external references without losing orientation.
key_checks: Test representative external links from the top nav and left reference rail such as Official docs, Branding, Open source, Checkout overview, Webhook quickstart, and Testing cards.
Confirm whether external destinations open in a sensible way relative to the local docs experience and whether returning to the local page is straightforward.
Use breadcrumb/home/local page links to recover context after visiting adjacent pages or external references.
Check whether repeated shared controls across pages behave consistently, especially search, top nav links, and the local section rail.
exit_criteria: A representative sample of external-reference links has been exercised from at least one page.
Recovery back to the local docs flow has been demonstrated after branching away from the primary content.

phases.title: Mobile responsiveness and touch usability
phases.objective: Repeat the highest-value flows on mobile to validate navigation, dense tutorial content, and the prescan-indicated tap target risks.
key_checks: On mobile, verify access to top navigation, local page switching, and search/dialog invocation from the hosted page.
Check whether long tutorial content remains readable without horizontal overflow and whether code blocks, tabs, and copy controls remain usable.
Specifically retest elements flagged with small tap targets where reachable: site home link, breadcrumb/title-style links, copy buttons, Yes/No controls, and bottom/reference links.
Confirm the mobile experience still supports movement between hosted, embedded, and customization pages without getting lost in the docs hierarchy.
Spot-check at least one adjacent page (embedded or customization) on mobile for the same shell consistency and interaction behavior.
exit_criteria: Critical hosted interactions have been repeated on mobile: navigation, search, one code tab interaction, and one copy action.
At least one additional local page besides index.html has been checked on mobile.
Any severe touch/usability regressions or layout breakages have been ruled in or out.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 3 known local HTML pages and scroll each enough to validate page-specific headings, tutorial structure, and shared shell behavior.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the major visible controls on the hosted page and representative shared controls on the other two pages: top nav, left rail navigation, search/dialog, code-language switching, copy buttons, in-page outline/scroll behavior, related cards, and a sample of external reference links.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the critical hosted flow and at least one adjacent-page check on a mobile viewport, with special attention to prescan-flagged small tap targets and dense code/tutorial sections.

notes: Do not spend disproportionate effort on external Stripe properties; use them mainly to assess link behavior and orientation/recovery.
Because the hosted page is the longest and most interaction-dense page, it should receive the deepest validation and most of the step budget.
No forms were detected, so prioritize navigation state, dialog behavior, content switching, clipboard feedback, and long-page wayfinding over form submission testing.

observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.

You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and borde

observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, }, ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", }); res.redirect(303, session.url); }); app.listen(4242, () => { console.log("Listening on http://localhost:4242"); }); Key Session parame

WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, }, ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", }); res.redirect(303, session.url); }); app.listen(4242, () => { console.log("Listening on http://localhost:4242"); }); Key Session parame

observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.PY Copy Showing Python import os import stripe from flask import Flask, redirect stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"] app = Flask(__name__) @app.post("/create-checkout-session") def create_checkout_session(): session = stripe.checkout.Session.create( line_items=[ { "price": "price_12345", "quantity": 1, } ], mode="payment", success_url="http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url="http://localhost:4242/cancel", ) return redirect(session.url, code=303) Key Session parameters for the hosted UI line_items The products or prices a customer is paying for. Stripe recommends usi

observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and borde

observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #edf2ff BUTTON COLOR #89a7ff TEXT COLOR #f5f8ff FONT FAMILY Source Code Pro BORDER SHAPE 10px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family

WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Ruby gem install stripe sinatra 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.RB Copy Showing Ruby require "sinatra" require "stripe" Stripe.api_key = ENV.fetch("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY") post "/create-checkout-session" do session = Stripe::Checkout::Session.create( line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, } ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", ) redirect session.url, 303 end Key Session parameters for the hosted UI line_items The products or prices a customer is paying for. Stripe recommends using saved Price objects whenever practical. mode Use payment for one-time purchases, subsc

observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Ruby gem install stripe sinatra 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.RB Copy Showing Ruby require "sinatra" require "stripe" Stripe.api_key = ENV.fetch("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY") post "/create-checkout-session" do session = Stripe::Checkout::Session.create( line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, } ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", ) redirect session.url, 303 end Key Session parameters for the hosted UI line_items The products or prices a customer is paying for. Stripe recommends using saved Price objects whenever practical. mode Use payment for one-time purchases, subsc

observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and borde

observation.title: Embedded Checkout page quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Php composer require stripe/stripe-php Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.PHP Copy Showing Php <?php require "vendor/autoload.php"; \Stripe\Stripe::setApiKey($_ENV["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"]); $session = \Stripe\Checkout\Session::create([ "line_items" => [[ "price" => "price_12345", "quantity" => 1, ]], "mode" => "payment", "ui_mode" => "em

observation.title: Embedded Checkout page quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.PY Copy Showing Python import os import stripe from flask import Flask, jsonify stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"] app = Flask(__name__) @app.post("/create-checkout-session") def create_checkout_session(): session = stripe.checkout.Session.create( line_it

observation.title: Embedded Checkout page quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.PY Copy Showing Python import os import stripe from flask import Flask, jsonify stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"] app = Flask(__name__) @app.post("/create-checkout-session") def create_checkout_session(): session = stripe.checkout.Session.create( line_it

observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and borde

observation.title: Embedded Checkout page quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.PY Copy Showing Python import os import stripe from flask import Flask, jsonify stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"] app = Flask(__name__) @app.post("/create-checkout-session") def create_checkout_session(): session = stripe.checkout.Session.create( line_it

observation.title: Embedded Checkout page quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.PY Copy Showing Python import os import stripe from flask import Flask, jsonify stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"] app = Flask(__name__) @app.post("/create-checkout-session") def create_checkout_session(): session = stripe.checkout.Session.create( line_it

WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and borde
