This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, }, ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", }); res.redirect(303, session.url); }); app.listen(4242, () => { console.log("Listening on http://localhost:4242"); }); Key Session parameters for the hosted UI line_items The products or prices

observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Search… / Menu Navigate Close LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and border_style Choose from Stripe’s supported font list and sup

observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Search… / Menu Navigate Close LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and border_style Choose from Stripe’s supported font list and sup

EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and border_style Choose from Stripe’s supported font list and sup

WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Search… / Menu Navigate Close LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and border_style Choose from Stripe’s supported font list and sup

observation.visible_text: stripe Search… / Menu Navigate Close LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and border_style Choose from Stripe’s supported font list and sup

observation.title: Embedded Checkout page quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Search… / Menu Navigate Close LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.PY Copy Showing Python import os import stripe from flask import Flask, jsonify stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"] app = Flask(__name__) @app.post("/create-checkout-session") def create_checkout_session(): session = stripe.checkout.Session.create( line_items=[ { "price": "price_12345", "quantity": 1, } ], mode

This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground.
